items.title: Equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model
items.physical_scope: An equation-based adoption for a specified smooth classical matter model on the selected oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. The matter current and stress are supplied by that model. This postulate does not assume a matter action, assert existence of solutions, include singular sources or establish empirical validity.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), curved Maxwell action and equations; §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), Einstein–Hilbert variation; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), Maxwell and scalar stress tensors. Source units and signs are converted to the local SI conventions.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.54)–(4.72), PDF pp. 120–125, Einstein–Hilbert and matter variations; Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, electromagnetic stress and coupling. Gaussian-unit and index conventions are not adopted.

items.title: Selected invariant matter-action contract
items.physical_scope: One actually selected smooth classical matter functional with compact variations in a fixed connection sector. Its Hilbert tensor and current are defined by the stated first-variation convention. No existence claim is made for arbitrary matter, and no measured matter model or coupled PDE solution is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.2–§4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), Hilbert stress and scalar/Maxwell matter examples. The action and compact variation assumptions here are stated explicitly.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147 (printed pp. 137–140), the on-shell diffeomorphism-invariance argument for stress conservation. The charged connection term is separately conditional here.

items.title: Interior stationary Einstein–Maxwell–matter action
items.physical_scope: A separately adopted interior variational formulation for smooth fields in a fixed bundle sector and one selected matter action. Only compactly supported variations, or variations vanishing near a physical boundary, are used. Boundary variational principles, singular self-fields, existence or uniqueness of coupled solutions, and empirical validity are not asserted.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), Einstein–Hilbert variation; §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), Maxwell action; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), matter and electromagnetic Hilbert tensors. The coefficients are restated in SI.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.54)–(4.72), PDF pp. 120–125, gravitational action, metric variation, and matter normalization; source normalizations are not imported.

items.title: Einstein–Maxwell equations from compact action stationarity
items.physical_scope: Conditional equivalence between compact interior stationarity of the adopted smooth fixed-sector action and its metric, connection, and selected matter Euler–Lagrange equations. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity improvement, empirical validity, or boundary variational principle.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), Maxwell action variation; §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), Einstein–Hilbert variation; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), stress conventions. The SI coefficients and compact-variation hypotheses are explicit here.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.54)–(4.72), PDF pp. 120–125, metric action variation and matter coupling. The assigned equations use the local SI and signature conventions.

items.title: Electromagnetic and matter stress exchange
items.physical_scope: Local stress exchange on smooth solutions of the adopted vacuum Maxwell system and one selected invariant matter action. The result is conditional on the matter fields being on shell. It asserts no global gravitational energy, Killing charge without symmetry and flux hypotheses, or coupled PDE solution.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.2–§4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), Hilbert stress, Maxwell stress, and diffeomorphism identity.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, electromagnetic stress; Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, on-shell diffeomorphism identity.

items.title: Restricted smooth charged-dust model
items.physical_scope: A restricted smooth continuum model with constant mass and charge parameters, positive proper number density, unit-normalized timelike velocity, number continuity, and the adopted Lorentz-force equation. It excludes caustics, singular particles and any coupled PDE existence claim.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–195 (printed pp. 183–188), Hilbert stress and continuum matter examples; the local dust closure and its validity limits are stated here.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, matter stress and diffeomorphism context; no dust action is inferred.

items.title: Charged-dust current and stress balance
items.physical_scope: A local deduction for smooth charged-dust fields satisfying the independently adopted number-continuity and Lorentz-force equations. It does not construct dust solutions, prove avoidance of caustics, or extend to singular particles.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–195 (printed pp. 183–188), stress and continuum-matter conventions. The dust product calculation is carried out under the local adopted closure.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, covariant stress-balance context. No matter-action existence is assumed in this proof.

items.title: Specified classical charged complex-scalar model
items.physical_scope: One classical smooth charged complex-scalar matter branch using the stated gauge-covariant functional and SI bookkeeping. It makes no quantum, statistical, material-response, empirical, or coupled-PDE existence claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), Abelian gauge field coupled to a complex scalar through a covariant derivative. Quantum and material claims are not adopted.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar matter action and Hilbert stress in curved spacetime.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, invariant matter action and stress conventions. The charged scalar formulas are specified by the exact local functional.

items.title: Field equations and balances of the selected scalar coupling
items.physical_scope: Conditional equations for one smooth classical charged-scalar functional coupled to the adopted smooth Einstein–Maxwell action. Current and stress balances hold on the scalar matter equation. No quantum interpretation, empirical matter claim, or coupled PDE solution is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), Abelian charged-scalar action and covariant derivative. The local current, stress, and balance identities are derived in the mathematical supplier.

references.locator: §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), metric variation; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar and Maxwell stress tensors.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, stress variation; Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, matter-on-shell diffeomorphism identity.

items.title: Background scalar wave versus coupled source equations
items.physical_scope: Exact smooth plane-wave calculations in the specified classical scalar model on a flat background. They distinguish a matter equation solution from a solution of the coupled equations and make no empirical or quantum claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), classical complex scalar and gauge-covariant derivative.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar-field stress convention; the displayed plane wave is checked locally.

references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, metric stress convention; the conditional calculation is explicit here.

items.title: A flat Maxwell field need not solve the coupled Einstein equations
items.physical_scope: A smooth exact counterexample showing that a source-free Maxwell solution on a prescribed flat background need not satisfy the coupled action-based Einstein equation. It uses no empirical data or singular field.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), curved Maxwell equations; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), electromagnetic Hilbert stress.

references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, Maxwell stress and Einstein coupling. The exact SI field is evaluated here.
